title_original: The Criterion Channel’s December Lineup Includes Christmas Crime, Jean-Pierre Melville, Speed Racer & More
excerpt_original: Good Christmas programming is hard to find. Amidst longtime favorites that aren’t actually any good and more-than-established classics, the Criterion Channel has replaced the treacly with the gritty in Christmas Crime—The Silent Partner, Ronin, Alan Rudolph’s Mortal Thoughts,…

blocks.text: Good Christmas programming is hard to find. Amidst longtime favorites that aren’t actually any good and more-than-established classics, the Criterion Channel has replaced the treacly with the gritty in Christmas Crime— The Silent Partner, Ronin , Alan Rudolph’s Mortal Thoughts , and Paul Verhoeven’s Elle among them. An easier pill to swallow (and doing what it says on the tin) are Hollywood Holiday Classics, offering a few of the best-known ( The Shop Around the Corner, Meet Me in St. Louis, Miracle on 34th Street ) and a few I simply don’t know ( Holiday Affair, Backfire, Desk Set ). Either way, I’ll try to impress family with whatever I pick on the morning of December 25.

For director retrospectives, six films by John Schlesinger, two from Jim Henson, eight Jean-Pierre Melville movies, three Sho Miyake films, and a ten-feature Olivier Assayas retrospective—including the rarely seen Disorder and Winter’s Child —play alongside Criterion’s Essential Fellini set. Restorations of Unzipped and Sisters, or the Balance of Happiness make streaming premieres, the latter included in a larger Margarethe von Trotta series also boasting films by Rainer Werner Fassbinder and Volker Schlöndorff. The former, meanwhile, is supplemented by Isaac Mizrahi’s Adventures in Moviegoing , itself complemented by fashion designer Jonathan Anderson’s own edition landing on December 15.

This is a big month for Criterion Editions: the new Wild at Heart disc and Leos Carax set, In a Lonely Place , To Die For , Sunday Bloody Sunday, Army of Shadows , and Shoah . On (needless to say!) a lighter note, 52 episodes of Speed Racer will be added to Criterion’s increasingly indispensable anime section. I’m also glad to see James Gray’s endlessly rewatchable We Own the Night land just as Paper Tiger arrives in theaters alongside Strange Days and The King of Comedy .
